utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: This sitting is now resumed. Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case IT-94-1-A-R77, the Prosecutor versus Dusko Tadic in a matter regarding allegations with regard to the prior counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. This morning we shall be taking evidence by videolink. Am I still in communication with everyone? I was saying that this morning we shall be taking evidence by videolink, coming from Banja Luka. May I take it that the appearances are as before? Then, Mr. Registrar, the next witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. The next witness is Milos Preradovic. He's now presently in Banja Luka, and we should have a satellite link but apparently from the noise I can hear on the line there are still some problems going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Are we in communication, Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, will the representative of the Tribunal administer to you the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milos Preradovic

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, your name is Milos Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would you tell us your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Will you tell us your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 10th of October, 1948.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prujanor or, rather, near Prujanor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Where do you live now? Mr. Preradovic, where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now I live in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What work do you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Retired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And before your retirement, what work did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before I retired I worked in the civilian police force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you give a statement to the Tribunal on 15th February, 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 15th of February? I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Will a representative of the Tribunal show you a statement dated 15 February, 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the transcript, this statement of the 15th of February, 1999 will be marked Exhibit 19. As to the other statement which was lodged with the Registry, this will be Exhibit 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not clear whether the witness recalls having given the statement dated 15 February, 1999. You have it now before you, Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. I do. Let me just read it. I've read the statement, but I didn't give it to you; I gave it to Dusko's brother, (redacted), in Prijedor, in the Balkan Hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Your correction is accepted. At the top I see the words "At the request of The Hague Tribunal", but you explained that you gave it to a certain person. Now, that is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That is the statement which you gave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That is the statement which you gave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the statement that I gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then unless there are any objections, the statement is admitted. No objections. Mr. Registrar, you'll mark it 19; is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Absolutely, Your Honour. This will be Exhibit 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: In that statement -- well, let me ask you this: Was this statement correct and true when you gave it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one that I gave in Prijedor, are you referring to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The statement which you just saw.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got a copy of the statement from (redacted) (redacted). That statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. I'm referring to the statement which is now on the ELMO and which you saw and which you say you gave. Were the contents of the statement true and correct when you gave that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the rest of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Interpreter, can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can hear the proceedings from the courtroom, but we didn't hear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You did not hear the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: -- we did not hear the end of the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Witness, did I hear you to say that the contents of that statement were true and correct when you gave the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The statement I gave to (redacted), yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, in that statement you refer to another statement which is attached --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before that, I signed a statement at the SUP in Prijedor, at the Commander's office, Commander Bozo Kos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, let me ask the representative of the Tribunal to show you Exhibit 18.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw it. I saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did you make that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, the statement that (redacted) gave me seemed different to me from this statement, and I did not receive a copy from (redacted) either.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Part of the answer could not be heard by the interpreters. The last bit was "... statement from the SUP."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, the interpreter did not hear the entirety of your answer. Would you kindly repeat the whole answer for her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first statement that I gave at the SUP was made in several copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: My question to you is this: Will you kindly look again at Exhibit 18? Would the representative of the Tribunal put it before you, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking at it right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is that your statement? Did you make that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that this is the accurate statement, the one I gave at the SUP, but I cannot say 100 per cent -- I cannot be 100 per cent sure because I did not get a copy from the SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would you look at the very top of that statement and, in particular, at the opening words "On the request of Mr. Milan Vujin ..." Do you see those words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did your statement to the SUP include those words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the contents of the statement did include those words, but I'm so sorry that I didn't take a copy of my own in the SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Very good, Mr. Preradovic. I would turn the matter over to counsel, who would ask you a few questions. First, some questions will be put to you by Mr. Abell, who is counsel for Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I actually ask any questions of this witness, in view of what he's just said, I'm going to ask if I can be given the opportunity to obtain another statement that this witness gave, which (redacted) has just told me about. I understand it is with the Court, and I hope that we will be able to lay our hands on it very quickly, but it may be important, given what this witness has just said. I'm sorry for the hiatus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Will this take some time, Mr. Abell?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I hope it won't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I have two statements to which reference has been made. I don't know if my colleagues have a third. I doubt it. They also are in my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: It is a statement that Your Honours may have seen before, I'm told, in connection with an additional evidence application. That's the one that I haven't got but am anxious to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: It is not before us today, I think. The legal officer explains to me that you're probably referring to a document filed, as you said, in a previous matter. She doesn't have it here, we don't have it here, but if you were to be so good as to give her details of it, she would try to retrieve it as soon as possible. Meanwhile, what do you propose, Mr. Abell? We have a videolink arrangement on --

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I very much appreciate it. It may be that -- I just thought that it may be that my friends can perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Maybe Prosecuting counsel can come to your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: We can, Your Honour. We have the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would that help you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: It would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: May I cast my eyes over it first?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Okay. Would you then be in a position to proceed on receipt of that document from Prosecution counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: May I just have five minutes to read it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I'm unaccustomed to the workings of the videolink arrangement. I don't know what the Registrar will advise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There's no problem with regard to the satellite link. We can remain in the courtroom, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Preradovic, Mr. Abell, counsel for Mr. Tadic, has requested a few minutes -- I was saying to Mr. Preradovic that Mr. Abell, counsel for Mr. Tadic, has requested a few minutes to look at a certain document, so do bear with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I'm very grateful for Your Honours' indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Abell is ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You have the floor, Mr. Abell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, have you seen (redacted) (redacted) before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Is he the one who came to my apartment in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes. Did he come and see you and take a statement from you on the 27th of December of 1998 in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he came and he wanted to take a statement, but please don't ask me for dates. I'm very bad at dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I'm going to show you on the ELMO the statement, and you can see the date, I hope, and your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: On the first page, can you see that it's headed "Statement of Milos Preradovic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Does it start by saying: "I, Milos Preradovic, born on the 10th of October, 1948, in Prujanor, want to give a statement in the case of Dusko Tadic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's the statement. That's it, and that's the beginning and the content of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: It was a detailed statement, wasn't it, went into quite a lot of detail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably. Well, you have it right in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes. Let's just look at the last page of the statement, just to see your signature and the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you raise it a bit more, please? To the left, please. To the left. Yes. Yes. That's my signature. I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You made that statement voluntarily, of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And you signed the bottom of each page of the statement, didn't you, as well as the end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: The statement was read to you before you signed it to make sure that you agreed with the contents of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And the statement that you gave to (redacted) in December of '98 was true and accurate when you made it, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Although I was in very poor shape and I was receiving an infusion precisely when the lawyer came, I think it's all right, that the statement was accurate, and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You would not have signed it, I suggest, if you had not been happy that it was accurate and true.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I probably wouldn't have been happy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: If it had been wrong, you wouldn't have signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Wouldn't have. I wouldn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you know somebody called Bogoljub Kos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Repeat this, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Do you know somebody named Bogoljub Kos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Does he come from Prijedor as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He's the Commander of the police station in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Did you go -- sorry. Did he come to you and ask you to go to the police station at Prijedor to look at a questionnaire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He called me on the phone and asked me to come to the SUP. He wanted me to have a look at something. He said that the lawyer Vujin had left a questionnaire, a statement, whatever. I cannot remember now because I did not receive a single copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: It was, I suggest, a questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A questionnaire or statement. I don't remember because of the four or five copies; I did not receive a single copy myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Let me see if I can refresh your memory. On the questionnaire, against your name, there was only one question, which was: "Did you or did you not see Mr. Dusko Tadic in Kozarac during the attack on Kozarac?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember the statement or questionnaire. I don't remember what it was called. Yes, it did say "Yes" or "No", did I or I did not see Dusko Tadic in Kozarac. Yes, that is what it said in the contents, and it coincides with the statements that I received later on from this lawyer, Vujin. Perhaps there are some --

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Let me please press on with my question. In answer to that single question on the questionnaire: "Did you or did you not see Dusko Tadic in Kozarac during the attack on it?", you said, "No," and you signed that questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And Mr. Kos asked you no further questions, no further details than that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The statement was in four or five copies. I don't remember exactly. The questionnaire or statement, whatever it was; I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I think you've told us you have never had a copy of that questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Mr. Vujin (sic), when did you first -- first of all, when, if you can help me, did you go and see Mr. Kos at the Prijedor police station and answer that question "No"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Could you give us a date for when you went to see Mr. Kos at Prijedor police station to answer "No" in the questionnaire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you -- I can't put a precise date to you -- that it might have been before February of 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly the exact date. My health situation was such that I forgot it. It was a mistake of me not to take a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Preradovic, did you see -- well, you tell us. When was the first time you ever met Mr. Milan Vujin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I met him -- I met him the first time when he brought me this statement. I think it was number 18. It was after the statement that I had signed to (redacted) -- for (redacted), (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: So you first met Mr. Vujin after the statement that is our Exhibit 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Could he please be shown that? He has one with him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the statement that I gave Vujin when I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Which is? Let me see if I can help you, Mr. Preradovic. You first saw Mr. Vujin -- you're showing us, I think, the statement you made on the 15th of February of 1999. That's the statement you gave to (redacted), isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And you first met Mr. Vujin after you gave (redacted) that statement on the 15th of February, 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: What did Mr. Vujin show you when he met you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He showed me this statement, the one that I'm showing you now, the one you're looking at now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: He showed you (redacted) statement, did he, the statement, that is, that you gave to (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We lost the first part of that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Let me start --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The statement that Vujin, the lawyer, showed me later on and the one I gave in the SUP are practically the same in content. It only differs in the "Yes" or "No". I can't remember that. Perhaps I didn't get the first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: The statement that Mr. Vujin showed you when he saw you after the 15th of February of 1999, was the statement he showed you the statement that you had given to (redacted) on the 15th of February, 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that those statements are similar, with the exception of the fact that I thought when (redacted) showed me, whether it was because of the photocopy or anything else, they weren't exactly the same. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Did Mr. Vujin show you what is our Exhibit 18 when he came to see you? That is the statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Could you have it up, please, on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Is that the statement that Mr. Vujin showed you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Can you put it up a bit? Yes, that's that statement that Vujin showed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Could you tell us where this meeting was with Mr. Vujin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With Mr. Vujin and another man who he came with from Prijedor. It was in front of my building; that is to say, the entrance next door to my building, in a cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Was the other man with him Mr. Saponja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: The father of Dragomir Saponja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: The father of Dragomir Saponja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what his son's name is. All I know is that he does have a son. I think he was Dragomir, but he played handball. I don't know his name exactly. He was a youngster.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: The man with Mr. Vujin was an older man, Mr. Saponja, the father of another Saponja.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was Slavko Saponja. I know him very well, but I don't know his son so well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Can you give us a date for that meeting, when Mr. Vujin and Mr. Saponja came to see you in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Let me see if I can help you. Would it have been about a month after you gave the statement to (redacted); in other words, in mid-March of 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was several days after I gave the statement to (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I suggest a month later, just about a month later. Does that sound about right, Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't quite remember, but it was a few days before I went. I think it was when I came to these same premises with (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: This may help you: Not long before the bombing began in 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We've lost him, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Not long --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was to come with (redacted) here to see (redacted). Well, a little before the bombing, yes. Sometime before the bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Now, were you going with (redacted) to pick up a witness summons to come to this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was informed -- I think it was during those couple of days, because that's when the lawyer Vujin came. Maybe it was on that same day, that very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Vujin, what was he saying to you when he came to visit you with Mr. Saponja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He gave me this statement and asked me if it corresponded to the statement that I made to Bozo Kos. I think it is similar to the other statement, but the contents weren't that familiar to me because I haven't got the first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Is this right: That the statement that you've seen in front of you today that says "On the request of Milan Vujin ...", Exhibit 18, is not the same piece of paper that you signed when you went into Prijedor police station and spoke with Mr. Kos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The contents of the statement are the same, almost the same, more or less the same. I'm not quite so sure, because I wasn't given a copy from the SUP in Prijedor, but the contents are more or less the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: My question was that the statement that you have in front of you, it's not the same piece of paper as the document you signed at Prijedor police station. Whether it's similar or not doesn't matter. It's not the same actual statement, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this statement has the same contents, everything is the same. I can't exactly remember, but I think that with Bozo there was something that said "Yes" or "No," and this same time hasn't got that "Yes" or "No." That's the only difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: If there's a difference between this statement and what you gave to Mr. Kos, it must be a different statement, it must be a different piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The paper's the same. It's the same format, everything is the same, and the contents of the statement, generally, it boils down to the fact of whether I saw Dusko Tadic. But I wrote to Vujin that the contents of the statement -- I noticed when Vujin left that in the statement, there isn't the "Yes" or "No" which did exist, I think, in the first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: So there is a difference between what you have been shown today, the piece of paper you've been shown today, and what you signed with Mr. Kos at Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, more or less, the statement is the same. The only thing is that "Yes" or "No," that worries me a little, just that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: That worries you because you remember saying that to Mr. Kos and it's not in the statement that you've had put in front of you today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, nonetheless, I made a mistake not to take a copy from Bozo Kos, and that is why now I am answering in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You rang up, didn't you, (redacted) (redacted) -- I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Let me change that. You rang up, didn't you, (redacted) on the same day or the day after Mr. Vujin had come to visit you, in March of this year, to tell him about that visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes. You spoke with (redacted), didn't you, in March of this year, on the same day that Mr. Vujin and Mr. Saponja came to visit you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm afraid we couldn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Let me ask the question again. You spoke to (redacted), didn't you, on the same day in March of this year when Mr. Vujin and Mr. Saponja came to visit you in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that that's how it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You told (redacted) that Mr. Vujin had shown you that statement, Exhibit 18, and was trying to convince you that it didn't really matter that it wasn't the same piece of paper because it was similar to what you had written to Mr. Kos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you say that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You told (redacted) about Mr. Vujin's visit to you at Prijedor with Mr. Saponja, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: There's a problem, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Obviously, the witness couldn't hear or did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Let me put it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You told (redacted) about Mr. Vujin and Mr. Saponja's visit to you in Prijedor, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You told (redacted) on the same day that Mr. Vujin and Mr. Saponja came to visit you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did tell him, because I came to Banja Luka with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You told (redacted) that Mr. Vujin had tried to convince you or persuade you that the statement that you now have in front of you, Exhibit 18, was similar to what you had signed at Prijedor police station with Mr. Kos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told (redacted) that Vujin and Saponja came to see me and that they gave me a statement ... and he said Kos and that I signed for Vujin that that could have been that statement. However, when they left and when I talked to (redacted), in this statement, I did not find a portion where it said "Yes" or "No," whereas the contents of the statement were more or less the same that I gave to Bozo Kos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: So when you looked at the statement with (redacted), you realised there was a difference, although they may have been broadly similar, that there was a difference.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The statements, both (redacted) statement and the one that I gave to Vujin and the one with Bozo Kos, as I say, the contents are almost the same; however, when I add all this up together, I feel -- I seem to feel that in Bozo Kos's statement, it said, "Did you see --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, the interpreter did not have the entirety of your last answer. Could you repeat it for her, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All three statements -- the last statement I gave to Vujin, they are almost the same in content, except for the fact that (redacted) statement that I signed there, it wasn't very legible, and that is why I said that it didn't correspond exactly. Whether it was the photocopy's fault or anything else, I don't know, but they're all more or less of the same content.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: We got cut off from you, Mr. Preradovic, in the middle of an answer you were giving, and I'm going to read it back to you because I want you to complete the sentence, if you can. Let me do my best to read it to you. "The statements, both (redacted) statement and the one that I gave to Vujin and the one with Bozo Kos, as I say, the contents are almost the same; however, when I add all this up together, I feel -- I seem to feel that in Bozo Kos's statement, I said, 'Did you see --'" Please finish that sentence off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: What was the difference you could remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that in the statement which is with Bozo Kos, there was a word "Yes" or "No," whether I had seen Tadic or not, and I answered --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Can you hear me again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Again, unfortunately, there was an interruption. Let me read your answer back. I asked you what was the difference that you could remember between what you said between Mr. Kos and Exhibit 18, and you said: "I think that in the statement which is with Bozo Kos, there was a word 'Yes' or 'No,' whether I had seen Tadic or not, and I answered --" Go on. Complete it. What did you answer to Mr. Kos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hello? Hello? I think that it said "Yes" or "No," and all the rest coincides with the last statement given to me by Vujin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You spoke on the 16th of March on the telephone, didn't you, with (redacted), the 16th of March of this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You told her as well about the fact that Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Just listen to the question. When you spoke with her on the phone, you told her as well, didn't you, that Mr. Vujin and Mr. Saponja had come to visit you in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And you told her that they had tried to convince you that the statement, our Exhibit 18, was similar to what you had written to Mr. Kos, what you had answered to Mr. Kos at Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told the lady that the contents of the statement given to me by the lawyer Vujin in the presence of Saponja, that it was the same contents as the Bozo Kos statement, except for that "Yes" or "No," but I can't remember anything now because I didn't get the first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Let me suggest, and I put to you, that what you told (redacted) was that when you saw Kos at Prijedor police station, there was only one question on the questionnaire, and all you had to do was say "Yes" or "No" and that was it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the top, the title, the heading of the statement, my own data about myself, Tadic's data --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- only that "Yes" or "No." I can't quite say because I did not get a single copy from Bozo Kos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You told her, I suggest, that the two documents were different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat, please? What two documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You told (redacted), (redacted), that the statement, our Exhibit 18, the one you have in front of you, and the questionnaire you'd answered for Kos, were different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember exactly that I put it that way, but I think that I said that I felt that just because of that "Yes" or "No", because of that. Just because of that "Yes" or "No", that there might have been a mistake there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Now look, please, and you may need to look on the ELMO, at the statement you gave to (redacted) in Prijedor on the 27th of December of '98.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know. I've looked at that statement and I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I'm looking --

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: If it helps Your Honours -- I think Your Honours now have copies -- I'm looking at the second last page of the typed copy. I'm going to take it from: "The reason that I never gave my statement before..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Can you see it there, Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I'm going to read it in English and you can hopefully follow it through as I read it: "The reason I never gave my statement before about those things is that I was absent due to my obligations on the front line during '95 and '96. I am sure if someone had tried to find me at that time, it would have been very difficult because of the war. I never met any of the lawyers of Dusko Tadic." In fact, pausing, the first lawyer of Mr. Dusko Tadic you actually met was (redacted), wasn't it, on the 27th of December of 1998, when you made this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I made a statement on the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And (redacted) was the first lawyer for Dusko Tadic that you had ever met, and you met him on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the first lawyer of Dusko Tadic whom I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And that obviously includes Mr. Milan Vujin, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milan Vujin. I met him after I had met this other one, the first lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: After you had met (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, after I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Thank you. I read on from the statement: "I never met any of the lawyers of Dusko Tadic. It is true that I received one telephone call from Mr. Vujin. It was a very short conversation. He only asked me if we could meet in connection with Dusko's case and nothing more."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: "Sometime after that, Commander Bogoljub Kos, from the station in Prijedor, called me in to the station because Mr. Vujin had left a questionnaire there in connection with Dusko Tadic, and if I agreed with the questions I should sign it. "There were four or five copies of the same questionnaire. Above my name there was only one question: Did I or did I not see Dusko Tadic in Kozarac during the attack on it? I answered "No," and signed it. Nobody ever asked me what happened in Kozarac on May 27th, 1992 or about the things I have just stated about before." That's what you said to (redacted), isn't it, in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, except for up there, the heading. The heading. Everything else coincides. This "Yes"/"No", that was, I think, in front of my name, where I was supposed to sign my name, I think, but I haven't got a copy so I can't guarantee anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Last question before we take a break. My question was that what I just read out to you and what you've seen on the screen, that is what you told (redacted) in your statement in December of last year, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't see any difference, and everything else -- what I said a moment ago. And this "Yes"/"No", I think it was in front of my signature, but I can't guarantee because I haven't got the copy. I haven't received a copy. But the contents of the statement is the same and it's just the heading, just the title. It says my name and Tadic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, would that be a convenient moment? I have a few more questions after the break, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, what will happen with the technical arrangements?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There is no problem whatsoever, Your Honour, and I do think that it is a good thing to have a break for the good health of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Preradovic, we will suspend the sitting for about 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The sitting is resumed. Are we in communication with Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Word has come that Mr. Preradovic has a medical appointment at 2 p.m. this afternoon. So it would be good if counsel, without doing any offence to his case, could expedite matters so that we finish with this witness in good time. I have in mind 1 p.m..

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I have nearly finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I'm still asking you questions, Mr. Preradovic. When you saw Mr. Kos at Prijedor police station, the only question you were asked about Mr. Tadic was whether you had seen him or not at the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether I had seen him? Where? In which village?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: On the questionnaire, Mr. Preradovic. Kozarac, the Kozarac village, the town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Dusko Tadic only twice during the war and both times in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes. What I'm asking you about is when you saw Mr. Kos, the only question you were asked about Mr. Tadic, Dusko Tadic, was whether or not you had seen him, "Yes" or "No", in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You weren't asked, I suggest, any details about any other names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I -- hello? Can you hear me? I made a mistake. I didn't take this copy. I'm telling you that in all honesty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: The questionnaire, you signed it, didn't you, the questionnaire, at Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm so sorry that I didn't take a single copy. Everything would be much clearer now. I don't know why they didn't give me this copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: The question was very simple. Did you sign the questionnaire at Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: What we have at Exhibit 18 is not a copy of what you signed at Prijedor police station.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the time being, I cannot remember that. However, the content is the same. There was a major difference in terms of years, but that's the content, except for this "Yes"/"No" thing, and that is what worries me now. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Abell, the witness has testified that the document which he signed at the police station had a "Yes"/"No" legend, and he recognises that that legend is not included in 18. Could you not leave it to the Tribunal to draw an inference as to whether the one document was the same as the other?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Let me deal with this, please: You made that statement on the 15th of February of '99 to (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And you made that statement to (redacted), didn't you, of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Would you have it in front of you, please, Exhibit 19?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: When you made that statement to (redacted), you were doing your best, weren't you, to tell (redacted) (redacted) the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Well, look at that statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm looking at it, and I've already read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You've read it. You make it clear in that statement, don't you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You make it clear in the statement, I suggest, to (redacted), that our statement, Exhibit 18, is a clear fraud, a clear forgery.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was a mistake in the photocopy or in something, I don't know what, but it seemed to me that it was not similar to this statement. However, now --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There's been an interruption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Of course, what happened between your making that statement to (redacted) in February of '99 and today, is your visit -- is the visit by Mr. Vujin and Mr. Saponja to your home in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before. Before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: No, that's wrong. I'm not going to go back over the evidence. We have already dealt with the dates. Let me put this to you: You remember I was asking you about what you told (redacted) when you spoke with her? You told her, didn't you, that whilst you would be prepared to give evidence of the truth in relation to Mr. Tadic, you did not want to get involved in saying anything that might hurt Mr. Vujin, the lawyer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already repeated what I had said. I said twice already that there were three statements, at Bozo Kos's, and at (redacted), and after that what Vujin brought. They approximately have the same content, except I haven't got the (redacted) statement or the SUP statement here with me, Bozo Kos's either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: My question was a very simple one. You told (redacted), on the phone, that whilst you were prepared to come to this court and tell the truth about Mr. Tadic, you were not prepared to get involved in giving evidence which might hurt the lawyer, Milan Vujin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't understand this lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You told her -- you told her as well, didn't you, that you had enough problems with your health without an extra problem of getting involved in giving evidence that might hurt Mr. Vujin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what you are referring to in terms of harming Mr. Vujin. I have my own health problems. What I'm doing now, testifying, is very hard for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I have to stand by everything I say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Abell, you referred to a statement made by the witness, dated 27 December, 1998, and I believe it was admitted as an exhibit. Is that right, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I would ask it to be if it hasn't actually been given the exhibit number yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. You would wish it to be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And may I suggest, having regard to the character of this statement, that it be put under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Prosecutor -- I better explain to Mr. Preradovic that now some questions will be put to you by Mr. Keegan for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, I'd like to go back to when you were called to the police station in Prijedor to look at this questionnaire. Prior to the time that you were called by Bogoljub Kos to come to the station, were you ever called by Mr. Vujin? Did you ever speak with Mr. Vujin on the phone prior to going to the Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did talk, but I do not remember when this happened. I told Mr. Vujin that I was not capable of testifying --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- testifying. So that's why I did not meet with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you recall whether, when you had this conversation with Mr. Vujin, it was before you went to the Prijedor police station and signed the questionnaire, or after?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I talked before I went to the police station, and later this questionnaire, statement, whatever, came in.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you remember what Mr. Vujin asked you about on the telephone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me whether I could testify about Dusko Tadic, because there were quite a few witnesses who were willing to testify. I said to him that I saw Dusko Tadic only twice during the war --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, we lost the last part of your answer, the part that came after you told Mr. Vujin that you saw Dusko Tadic only twice during the war, and we lost what came after that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko Tadic, I saw him only twice in Prijedor. Where I live --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that's why I could not make any statement to Mr. Vujin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did Mr. Vujin ask you to go to the police station to sign the questionnaire or statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember that he asked me to do so. He gave Bogoljub Kos that questionnaire so that Bogoljub Kos could call me in to sign this. I didn't even know what it was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was it Bogoljub Kos who told you that Mr. Vujin had given him the questionnaire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I think that it remained with him. This is quite a long period, so I cannot remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, you stated earlier that there were four or five copies of this questionnaire that you saw at the Prijedor police station. Do you recall whether all of the copies were the same; that is, were they the exact same document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the same content. All of it is the same. I signed all of them, but unfortunately I did not take any copies for myself, and that is, unfortunately, why this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, then, that you looked at and read all four or five copies, however many there were, before you signed them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, did all of the copies contain that reference to the question with the "Yes" or "No" answer block in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes, because --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, we lost your last answer. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On all these questionnaires, or statements, I mean, the content was the same, and above my signature there was this "Yes"/"No" thing. I cannot guarantee it because I haven't got a copy with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you have a copy of what is marked as Exhibit 18 in front of you that's in the Serbian language; that is, the copy with your signature on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you please confirm for the Court, is that your signature that appears on that document below your name or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When, to the best of your recollection, did you sign this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When is it that you signed this document, Exhibit 18?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I signed it when Slavko Saponja came with the lawyer to Prijedor, the beginning of 1998. I can't remember the date. It was mentioned at the beginning of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I'd like to refer to the meeting with (redacted) (redacted). Is it your testimony that you are not sure whether the statement which (redacted) showed you was either the same statement you signed in the Prijedor police station or the same as the statement which you signed for Mr. Vujin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that almost all of the statements are identical, almost. Only in the case of the (redacted) (redacted) statement, which I did not get, just like I didn't get the one in the SUP, I don't know whether it was a question of having it retyped or something, but all the statements boil down to the same thought, all three statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did (redacted) tell you where he obtained or where he got the copy of the statement which he showed to you on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You cannot remember if he told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot. Mr. Prosecutor, I cannot remember. I'm not feeling too good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I will try to be brief, Mr. Preradovic. In this statement which you gave to (redacted) which we have before us, that statement --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've got it too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Fine. If you could look at that statement as I ask you the following questions: In that statement, it says that the statement that you're being shown by (redacted) is not consistent with the statement which you signed in Prijedor police station and in the presence of the chief of police, Bozidar Kos, presumably Bogoljub Kos. What did you mean by it's not consistent with the statement that you signed in the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that perhaps there was a mistake in the copying of the statement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- perhaps this condition of mine affected me too. However, all three statements are similar, and what I wrote for Tadic, I believe that perhaps in terms of the copy or the format or whatever, you know, in that sense, that's how I wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The penultimate sentence in that statement you gave to (redacted) is quite declarative. It says: "I am confirming that this statement," meaning the one shown to you by (redacted), "is a clear fraud and that I never gave such a statement." Did you, in fact, say that to (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you, perhaps it's a mistake in the copying of the statement that I had with me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- "Yes" or "No," perhaps in connection with this "Yes" or "No." I can't remember whether it was there, so that's why I stated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, when Mr. Vujin came to see you and he showed you Exhibit 18 and you signed that document, did you tell Mr. Vujin that the statement he was showing you was different from the one that you signed in the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told Mr. Vujin in writing, and I signed this, that the statements were identical approximately. That's what I think. However, I forgot to mention to Vujin as well that it seemed to me that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Vujin, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise to my learned friend, Mr. Keegan. I don't want to make any suggestions, but I think that a small error has occurred with regard to Mr. Keegan's question related to Exhibit 18 today. Because in response to Mr. Keegan's question, it was said that Mr. Preradovic signed this document when I visited him in March this year. So could you please clear up this matter? I presented this document as a document that was signed in the police station, at Kos's, and when I showed this document to Preradovic, it had already been signed by him, and Mr. Preradovic is talking about another document that you don't know about yet; however, during our examination, you're going to find out. So could you please clarify this matter so that there wouldn't be any confusion? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Vujin, in addition to an opportunity to examine the witness, you will have an opportunity to present your own evidence on the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, let me first then return back to Exhibit 18, and again I'd like you to look at the copy you have before you, which is in your own language and is signed by you. Once again, when is it that you signed that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Court when you signed that document, the approximate date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, what document are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Exhibit 18, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I have information, Mr. Keegan, that the date at the top of the document was inserted by an officer of the Tribunal --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: -- and the document was likely to be signed before that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but there is no date on the actual Serbian version, and I'm trying to see if the witness can tell us when he recalls signing the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, do you recall my question and can you answer it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It appears we may have lost the signal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: This has happened before. I do not surrender all hope. What do you say, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. I think that ideally we should just be patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, referring to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: -- Exhibit 18, can you confirm for the Court whether or not you signed this document in 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you referring to the document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I'm referring to the document marked Exhibit 18, which is the document that begins "On the request of Mr. Milan Vujin, defence counsel of Dusko Tadic, I give the following statement ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That statement? That statement was signed by -- it was signed this year, it seems to me, when Saponja came to see me in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, there are only three exhibits that have been introduced this morning: Exhibits 18, 19, and 20. Exhibit 18 is the document we have been referring to just now in my questions, Exhibit 19 is the statement which you gave to (redacted), and Exhibit 20 is the statement which you gave to (redacted). We have reason to believe that Exhibit 18 was signed sometime prior to 5 February, 1998. Do you have any recollection of signing such a document prior to 5 February, 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The evidence -- material evidence and the statement by Mr. Vujin is this last one that I have in front of me, and not the one from the SUP, which was signed this year, but I don't remember exactly when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I should explain that to prevent the parties from being misled, I made the statement which I did make about the insertion by an officer of the Tribunal of that date. If the parties are disagreed about that, then evidence could be led on the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I don't have anything further, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Abell?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before there's any further cross-examination, it may be sensible to elicit in some way, shape, or form that the document that the witness in Banja Luka has in front of him, Exhibit 18, must be a photocopy and that he's not looking at any original. I assume that to be the case. It may be important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The Tribunal gives you leave to ask one question on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Further questions by Mr. Abell:

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, you've been asked some questions about Exhibit 18. That's the statement which begins "On the request of Mr. Milan Vujin ..." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "At the request of the lawyer, the defence counsel for Mr. Dusko Tadic," that is the statement I have before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, no, no. On the request of Mr. Milan Vujin, Exhibit 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the Serbian language, this statement reads as it was read out by the witness, Mr. Preradovic. Perhaps the translation is a little different and that is why this has come about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I thought as much, Mr. Domazet. Mr. Abell, I believe that the problem is that we're dealing with different languages, but the substance is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I'm very grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You and I are looking at the same exhibit. Do you still have it in front of you, Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it. I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That document that you have in front of you, it is a photocopy, isn't it? It is not the original document, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Has it got your signature on it, Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is that the original signature or a copy of your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My signature, the one I signed, but it's probably a copy, but it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to establish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: I have several questions to ask before Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You must elect whether the questions will be put by you or Mr. Domazet. Which will it be? You will put all the questions or will Mr. Domazet put the questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: In this case, when it is a question of this witness, I am going to ask the questions because I have been given leave to head my own defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All that the Chamber wanted to know is whether you would be asking the questions or Mr. Domazet. Fine. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If you wish, I can show you the original of the statement that has been designated with the number 18, if anything is being contested. If it isn't, then we can continue immediately. So that you can compare it to the copy which Mr. Preradovic himself has.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't want Mr. Vujin to be under any misapprehension at all. On behalf of Mr. Tadic, the authenticity of the document, Exhibit 18, is very much in issue. In our submission, it is a forgery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Vujin is doing the correct thing in making the original available to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: In case there is any question about it. There is --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Could I offer the Court another statement by Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If you so wish, Your Honour, it might be good to give an exhibit number for the original. The original would be 18C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Very good. I take it that the Registrar would make photocopies available to the parties?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but you know that the copy of it has already been given to the parties because this is Exhibit 18, and I can only show you the original, because otherwise, if I make photocopies, they will become copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: No. There is a question as to whether those copies are the same as this original. So would you kindly make copies of this exhibit available to the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a copy of that document, sufficient examples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Vujin, on this occasion we could relieve you of that responsibility and ask the Registrar to make copies. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might. The question is: Do those copies have original signatures or are they photocopies of the signatures as well? In other words, did he sign more than one copy, is what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: No, he signed the original copy of the original. The copy of the original has the signature. I would now like to offer, before I ask the questions, because there has been -- I think the mistake there is I have the original of the statement by Mr. Preradovic, dated the 15th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I mean no disrespect to interrupt, but I must express considerable concern about what is now taking place. Mr. Vujin is the accused in relation to -- I'm sorry to be blunt about it, but he is -- in relation to these contempt proceedings. He has elected to have counsel appear with him, and as I understood Your Honours' ruling right at the outset, Mr. Vujin was allowed right of audience. I have no complaint as to the court's decision in relation to that. Either he or Mr. Domazet can elect, therefore, to cross-examine witnesses. I don't object to that. What I'm very concerned about, with the greatest of respect, is it sounds as if what we are getting is either a speech or evidence from Mr. Vujin, and not only that, but evidence or a speech that this witness is presumably listening to on the video, and I would respectfully submit that if Mr. Vujin wants to, in due course, give evidence, the appropriate time is not now. If he wishes to ask questions, that's a different matter. Forgive me for interrupting but, in my submission, we must be very careful here indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: We'll explain to Mr. Vujin that his function at this time is limited to asking questions, but if he wants to put in material through this witness in the normal way, I don't see any objection to that course. Yes, Mr. Vujin. Please limit your questions to questions which could be answered by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can I now ask directly, ask Mr. Preradovic directly something? Can Mr. Preradovic hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, when I visited you in Prijedor with Mr. Saponja, that was on the 15th of March, 1999, exactly on the day when you were to leave for Banja Luka. Did I, on that occasion, ask you, when I showed you the statement which you signed at Bozo Kos's, to write several -- give us several examples of your signature and to confirm that that is your signature so as to be able to compare that signature with the signature you placed on the statement at Bozo Kos's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did I leave you a copy of that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Have you got a copy of that statement with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't got it with me. I have it at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Could we now show that statement to Mr. Preradovic, dated the 15th of March? I have enough copies here in English and Serbian, and the original as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: I would like to have this shown to witness Preradovic now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Can you see the document, Mr. Preradovic, dated the 15th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have this one in front of me, but I can't see yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Can you see the text, the statement of the 15th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: On the text that you can see, in the upper left-hand corner are there four signatures there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Focus in, please, on the document, the upper half. I can't see the upper half. I can see my signature, but I want to see the upper part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Are those your signatures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Can you read what it says underneath those signatures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you put the document up a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Would you read it out aloud, please, Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you bring it up closer? Could I have a close-up, please? "For my signatures to be used for the statement that I gave to a lawyer, Mr. Vujin, at Bozo Kos's." Then the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: And the signature on the right hand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did you write this in your own hand, all of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: When I requested you to write down your signature several times and to confirm this, did I exert any pressure on you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, you did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did I ask you to sign anything else apart from that? Can you hear me, Mr. Preradovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you once again to confirm whether the signatures, the four signatures in the upper part of the document, are your own signatures and whether the signature at the bottom of the document is your signature as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vujin, all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did you, at any time, because you've said that you didn't have any contact with the lawyers of Dusko Tadic, did you at any time talk to Mr. Miodrag Kostic sometime in February 1996, who was the investigator of the Tribunal; that is to say, of the former Defence counsel of Mr. Tadic? Did Mr. Kostic have a talk with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: You don't remember. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Vujin, may I ask you to pause to inquire whether-- it's now a little after 1.00, and information has reached me as to the necessity for Mr. Tadic to go somewhere for awhile, and we have also on our hands the fact that Mr. Preradovic has a medical appointment. So it's either we finish within a few minutes or we go over to the afternoon, and then I don't know how Mr. Preradovic will stand for that. What's your position? Will you be much longer?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have concluded the questioning of Mr. Preradovic. I just need two minutes to give the court two more exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then may I ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: -- if it is all right for his client to leave the room now? I believe his client wishes to leave the room now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: May I just take instructions if that's correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Just one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You accept the proceedings go on in his absence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: On the day that I came to you and asked you to sign me -- give me several examples of your signature, did I give you, at your request, a photocopy of your statement, the one you made at Bozo Kos's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this way: Yes, you did give me the statement, but I said to the lawyer beforehand, Tadic's present lawyer, that I seem to feel there was -- but the contents are the same.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There was an interruption, we apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: All I asked you was whether I left you with a copy of that statement. Did the copy stay with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I received a copy of the statement, yes, but -- that is to say, this one, but I think that they are the copies that I signed at Bozo Kos's, but the contents are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: So those are the copies at Bozo Kos's which I transmitted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't got a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Yes. Just one more question for you, Mr. Preradovic. When we spoke over the phone and when you said that you wouldn't be able to testify, did you, at that moment or a little beforehand, were you in hospital, and was that the reason that you were not able to come and testify, because of your illness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On one occasion I was outside Prijedor. On the second occasion I was in hospital, but I don't quite remember, but I was absent for valid reasons both times.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just this thing now. Vujin, can I go on a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour, for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd like to ask leave to ask one question about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would you be long?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: One question only, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You're aware of the problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.
