utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I should perhaps inquire from the interpreters whether they're agreeable to our proceeding for another few minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic, I'd like to ask you one further question about Exhibit 18, which is the statement headed, "On the question of Mr. Vujin, the Defence counsel of Dusko Tadic". You still have that document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, do you recall ever signing more than one copy of this particular statement, this particular document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one I have before me here? Number 18 you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, when you signed that statement, on the occasion that you signed it, do you remember if you signed more than one copy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I did at Bozo Kos's. I did sign there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, when Mr. Vujin was cross-examining, the witness indicated -- was in the middle of an answer, and I wrote this down: "I said to Tadic's present lawyer that I can't," and then he was, with respect to Mr. Vujin, interrupted, and we never got the end of that answer. I'm afraid the LiveNote transcript has moved up the page and I don't know how to get it down again, but it may be of assistance to the Tribunal to hear what that answer would have been if Mr. Vujin hadn't cut it short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would Mr. Preradovic like to answer that question briefly?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, just bear with me whilst we try to get the LiveNote back to the relevant passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Vujin, the Chamber will give you a chance in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Let me try without the aid of a note. May I, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Mr. Preradovic -- Mr. Preradovic, can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Do you remember Mr. Vujin asking you some questions a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Do you remember Mr. Vujin asking you questions a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember him asking me questions in relation to what I signed at his place. I don't remember the other questions. I remember as far as the signatures go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Abell, is it possible to put to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is. The LiveNote is now coming and I'm trying to get the accurate question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You were asked this question by Mr. Vujin: Q On the day that I came to you and asked you to give me several examples of your signature, did I give you, at your request, a photocopy of your statement, the one that you made at Bozo Kos's? And your answer was: A Well, let me tell you this way. Yes, you did give me the statement, but I said to the lawyer beforehand, Tadic's present lawyer ... Pause there, Mr. Preradovic. Do you mean (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic's present lawyer. You said you told Mr. Tadic's present lawyer something about the statement. Did you mean by "present lawyer", (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know, in concrete terms, what that refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: All right. You went on in your answer: A I told -- I said to the lawyer beforehand, Tadic's present lawyer, that I seemed to feel that there was ... You were referring to the statement. What did you seem to feel? Seemed to feel that there was what, and you were interrupted. Seemed to feel that there was what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Abell, the court has been very flexible with you. The court might have taken the position that you ought, at the proper time, to have intervened on that. Now, Mr. Vujin.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am concluding, by tendering another document, and that is an expert opinion as to the identity of the signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: May I ask you to reserve that for the time when you're giving evidence, because at this stage we're only concerned with questioning the witness. But you will have a full opportunity --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, let me see if my colleagues have any questions. Only one little question, Mr. Preradovic, if you're there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I gather from you that there was no material inconsistency between the statement which you made to Kos and this statement which you gave to Mr. Vujin. Then can you tell us why you troubled to make this statement to (redacted), dated 15th February, 1999? Why did you feel it necessary to make that statement to (redacted) if you thought that there was no contradiction between the statement which you gave to Mr. Kos and the statement which you gave to Mr. Vujin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way: The statement I gave to (redacted), it is the same -- the contents are the same as the other one, except that with (redacted) statement, I seem to think that something was not very clear, either in the copy or something else, and that is why I gave this, and I don't know why I should have given the statement at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. That's the same question that I'm asking myself. Thank you very much. Well, we're through with this witness, are we? Then the witness is excused and we will suspend the sitting until 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.18 p.m. 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: May I take the opportunity of announcing, for the convenience of all, that tomorrow we shall work from 9.30 to 1 p.m. with a coffee break. We will not be able to sit during the remainder of the day. So 9.30 to 1.00. Call in the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can hear you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Your name is Sasa Maric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Will you kindly take the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand that. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Do be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Witness B, will you tell us where you were born and when?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: I was born in Banja Luka on the 1st of February, (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What work do you do?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: A waiter in Bosna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, did you make a statement, a written statement, in this case? I will ask the Registrar to show you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This will be Exhibit 24, which is filed with the Registry under the number 5131.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Have a look at this statement and see if that is the statement you made.

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: When you made this statement, the contents were true and correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: The truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The signature at the bottom is your signature?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The contents of the statement are still true today?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then I would ask you to take some questions from Mr. Abell, counsel for Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: You speak in your statement of an occasion at the Bosna Hotel when you were joined by (redacted), and a little later you were joined by the lawyer Milan Vujin and another lawyer, Simo Tosic.

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Mr. Tosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And that there was a conversation involving all of you, where you all sat together; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: That's right. But I was only a guest there with (redacted); I kept him company.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And (redacted) was speaking to you about some problems that he'd had?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Well, he said that he was being threatened, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Mr. Vujin spoke, telling him not to worry about it and that if need be, he, (redacted), could come to Mr. Vujin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: And (redacted) spoke then of (redacted) (redacted), saying that he had spoken to them about it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Now, you say that Mr. Simo Tosic then said something. Remind us. What did he say? What did Mr. Tosic say about that, when (redacted) (redacted) were mentioned?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: To have as little contact as possible with foreign lawyers. Because they were foreign lawyers, he should have as little contact as possible with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Where was Mr. Vujin when Mr. Tosic said that?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: We were sitting at the same table.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: How close was he to Mr. Tosic when that was said by Mr. Tosic?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Well, we were sitting at a round table -- a square table, a round table.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: What was Mr. Vujin's reaction, if anything, when Mr. Tosic said that?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: A normal reaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Did he in any way appear to disagree with Mr. Tosic, with his saying that he should have as little contact with (redacted) as possible because he was a foreign lawyer?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: There were no comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: To make sure that we've understood this correctly, would that have been in the summer of 1998, last summer?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Can you remember if it was early or late summer?

utterances.speaker: Witness B.
utterances.text: Sometime in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: That's all I ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Before you begin, Mr. Keegan, Mr. Registrar, did we give a number to this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Twenty-four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Twenty-four. We admitted it as an exhibit? There are no objections, I take it? No objections. Fine. The record has been straightened out. Thank you. Mr. Keegan, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: We have no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: No questions. Well, I will not say that the bench is disappointed. I think we may excuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Demand has outstripped supply this afternoon. We don't have another witness. So until tomorrow at 9.30, and we will then adjourn until that moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: 5.38 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 3rd day of September, 1999, at 9.30 a.m.
